(By Sri. Dattatreya.M.Joshi., Adv)
 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic accident.
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 23.07.2022 at about 2.45 a.m., the Petitioner was proceeding on a bike bearing No.KA-02-KB-8929 as a pillion rider, the same was ridden by its rider by name Suresh Kumar.K and Petitioner's relative by name Rakshith was on his bike towards Koratagere, when they reached near Tannenahalli, on Urdigere-Koratagere road, Kolalal Hobli, Koratagere Taluk, Tumkur, the petitioner relative's bike i.e.,
Rakshith's got mechanical problem, hence Suresh Kumar parked the bike on the extreme left side of the said road, after attending the mechanical problem at about 3.00 a.m in order to move towards Koratagere, the petitioner was sitting back seat and Suresh Kumar.
K was about to move ahead, at that time the driver of Swift car bearing reg No. KA-05-AH-3387 came from Urdigere side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against bike.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was admitted to Government Hospital, Tumkur, wherein he was taken first aid, thereafter he was shifted to Spine Care & Ortho Care Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was taken treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

entities.text: Spine Care & Ortho Care Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as Agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of Swift car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. Despite service of notice the Respondent No.1 remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed its objection.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Nagaraju G.C vs Ramesh B.L on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177680177/
2 car.
Further it contended that the accident was caused solely due to carelessness and negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and thereby caused the accident.
It has admitted the issuance of the policy.

Further it contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and also does not have proper and valid FC to use the vehicle on the road.

Further it contended that the rider of the motor cycle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and also does not have proper vehicle documents like RC, emission and insurance policy.
Further it contended that the accident occurred due to the reckless and rash and negligent manner of the driver of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KB- 8929.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 23.07.2022 at about 3.00 a.m on Urdigere-Koratagere road, near Tannenahalli Koratagere Taluk, Tumkur, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Swift car bearing No.KA-05-AH-3387?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.15.
Thereafter, the petitioner got examined 4 witnesses as PW.2 to P.W.5 and got marked document as per Ex.P.16 to 26 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for Petitioner and the learned Counsel for Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 23.07.2022 at about 3.00 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05- AH-3387 by its driver.
10.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AH-3387 by its driver.

Nagaraju G.C vs Ramesh B.L on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177680177/
3 11.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-15.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to 8 are the true copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate,
Charge sheet.
Ex . P.7

& 8 are the discharge summaries, Ex.P.9 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar card of PW.1, Ex.P.10 is the Photographs, Ex.P11 is the CD, Ex.P12 is the Medical bills, Ex.P.13 is the Advance receipts, Ex.P.14 is the Medical prescriptions, Ex.P.15 is S-ray.
Ex.P.16 to 26 are medical records.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.1 and 2 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Kolala.P.S, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of Swift car bearing Regn.No.KA-05-AH-3387 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar which shows that when petitioner and his relative about to move on their bike, the driver of Swift car bearing reg No. KA-05-AH-3387 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against bike.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects of the Motor vehicle.
The damages found on both vehicle justifies the involvement of the vehicles in the accident.
The Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The Ex.P.6 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Kolala Police have Charge-sheeted the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.338 and 279 of IPC.
Ex.P.7 and 8 are the discharge summaries which show that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for the injuries sustained in the RTA.

13. Further, Petitioner has examined Dr. Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P.16 and 17 i.e.,
Clinical notes and X- ray film.
He deposed about the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident and assessed the disability.

Three Medical record Officers got examined as PW.3 to PW.5 and got marked Exs.P.18 to 26 i.e., authorization letter, Case sheet, Notarized copy of ID card and MLC register extract, Office order dated 16.01.2025, MLC register extract, original police intimation letter, OP registration card, X-ray film.
These documents show about the treatment taken by the petitioner.
14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2.
Nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
Though the respondent No.2 contended that the accident did not occur due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car, it has not adduced any evidence to rebut the evidence of petitioner.
Moreover, the charge sheet is the material document, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and the documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the Petitioner has proved that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-AH-3387 and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15. Issue No.2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Nagaraju G.C vs Ramesh B.L on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177680177/
4 16.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 65 years.
He has produced Aadhar card which is marked at ExP.9 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card his date of birth is shown as 01.01.1957.
The accident has taken place on 23.07.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 65 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
17. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was doing as Agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove avocation and income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
19.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.5 wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Right Ankle fracture dislocation.
2. Medial malleolus, posterior malleolus 3. Fracture with proximal fibula fracture
Further, the Doctor has opined that the said injuries grievous are in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
20. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
21.

The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 23.07.2022 to 28.07.2022 and 22.02.2023 to 25.02.2023 at Spine Care & Ortho care Hospital, Bengaluru and he was underwent surgery.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, P.W.2 Dr. Nagaraj.B.N has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
The discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.7 and 8 also justify the same Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 8 days.
Nagaraju G.C vs Ramesh B.L on 9 April, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177680177/
5 22. Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken to him and his age, he might have taken at least three months for recovery.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.46,500/- under this head (@ Rs.15,500/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
23.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.

V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
24.
The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 66 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.12 which is totally amounting to Rs.1,07,487/-.
I have gone through the medical bills.
The bills are issued by the tread hospital.
Moreover there is no serious dispute about the medical bills.
Hence, the bills are accepted.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,07,500/- as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

25. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he cannot walk, cannot stand and sit on floor, cannot do manual work and often getting headache due to head injury and he cannot concentrate on his work since injuries cost or permanent in nature.
26. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, he got marked Clinical notes and X-ray at Ex.P.16 and Nagaraju G.C vs Ramesh B.L on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177680177/
6 17.
He assessed total disability of right lower limb at 42% and whole body disability at 14%.
27. In the cross-examination, PW.2 has admitted that petitioner underwent ORIF.
Implants are removed.
Fractures are united.

28. It is pertinent to note that when the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner is considered in the light of the deposition of PW.2, it can safely be said that there is a functional disability of 14%.

The petitioner had sustained right ankle fracture dislocation with medial and posterior malleoulus fracture and he was treated with ORIF with LCP for the medial malleoulus and CC screws and SS wire for posterior malleolus and as such the permanent physical disability stated by PW.2 at 14%
can be held to translate into the functional disability of 15%.
29. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 7.

With multiplier of 7, income of Rs.15,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 14%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,82,280/- (Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 7 x 14/100 = Rs.1,82,280/-) which is rounding off Rs.1,82,300/- Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,82,300/- under this head.
TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
30.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.1,07,500/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 46,500/-
laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.1,82,300/ Total Rs.4,54,300/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,54,300/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

31. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Swift car bearing Reg.

Nagaraju G.C vs Ramesh B.L on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177680177/
7 32.
There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car in question.
There is no dispute of the fact that the policy in respect of said vehicle was valid and effective as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
33. ISSUE No.3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for total  compensation of Rs.4,54,300/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, the entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

30.

Medical expenses Rs.1,07,500/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 46,500/-
laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.1,82,300/ Total Rs.4,54,300/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,54,300/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for total  compensation of Rs.4,54,300/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After the deposit of the Award amount and interest being made by the Respondent No.2, the entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
